newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 23.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohammad of Malaysia told the visiting Bangladesh Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad in Kuala Lampur that his country wanted to make large-scale investment in Bangladesh.
Foreign Secretaries of India and Bangladesh are due to hold a three-day meeting in New Delhi beginning Monday to chalk out policy decisions to eliminate cross-border insurgency and crime.
The Ministry of Land has planned new projects to rehabilitate 20,000 families living in slums in Dhaka.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said an excellent environment exists now in Bangladesh for free trade under a liberal and dynamic regime.

The West Bengal Congress has conferred on Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina the "Netaji Memorial Award" in recognition of her role in promoting "peace, democracy and fraternity in the sub-continent".
Finance Minister S A M S Kibria on Saturday expressed concern over the slow recovery of classified loan and asked the bankers to apply the new law framed to deal with the default menace.
An 11-member trade delegation from Britain, the second in a month, arrived in Dhaka on Saturday to explore business opportunities in Bangladesh.
Acute scarcity of sugarcane across the country has forced six sugar mills to cease their operations far ahead of schedule.
